title: Choosing Recessed Light Bulbs: Incandescent, Halogen, CFL, and LED
summary: This video from This Old House compares common recessed-light bulb options, explaining what each bulb type is, how it’s installed in recessed fixtures, and practical considerations such as heat, ballast technology, upfront cost, lifespan, and long‑term energy savings. It covers incandescent, halogen (MR16), compact fluorescent (CFL) with a four-pin plug-in, and LED recessed lights. The hosts note that electronic ballasts reduce CFL flicker and buzz, describe LED as a circuit-board light source, and contrast initial price against longevity and electricity use, highlighting LED’s substantial efficiency advantage despite higher upfront cost.
topics: Fluorescent recessed light (CFL) with four-pin plug-in
Bulb cost and lifespan: incandescent (~$5, 2-3 years)
Halogen cost and lifespan (roughly similar to incandescent)
Energy efficiency: wattage comparisons (65W incandescent vs 10W LED)
